svg.title: The low-order terms fit this same estimate because x−30 ≤2Ω1/200(x)s5−j for 0 ≤j ≤4. The final inequality follows from s5 = x−5/2 times a fixed subpower factor, whereas σx = x−1−1/100Ω2(x). Thus the fifth-order Taylor remainder has a strictly decaying power to spare. The finite-difference surgery uses h = θx−1/24. Since h/s ≤x−1/24, choosing its order m ≥48 makes every fixed subpower multiple of s(h/s)m+1 at most σxh eventually. This controls the surgery error after division by its difference step. The support margins and nonwrapping conditions used here are the finite chart conditions already imposed when choosing the station; none is a new continuum hypothesis.
